text: Who's behind Market Watch? In this video, I'm going to share my journey — almost 25 years building trading systems at some of the world's biggest financial institutions. Let's get into it.

Almost 25 years. That's how long I've been working in financial markets — not as a trader, but as the person building the technology that makes trading possible. From real-time data feeds to order matching engines, from risk systems to algorithmic platforms.

Here's what we'll cover today. My career path across exchanges, banks, data providers, and hedge funds. Why understanding market infrastructure gives you a unique edge as a trader. How Market Watch was born and what makes it different from typical trading channels. And the vision — bringing institutional-grade tools to everyone, for free.
Chapter two. The professional journey. Let me take you through the institutions where I spent nearly 25 years building the backbone of global markets.

It all started with a simple fascination. I studied engineering, but what really drew me in was financial markets. The complexity, the speed, the global scale. I knew I wanted to be as close to the action as possible — and building the technology was the way in.

Thomson Reuters. One of the largest financial data providers in the world. I worked on real-time market data infrastructure — the feeds that power literally every trading desk on the planet. When you see a stock price update on your screen, there's an entire pipeline behind it. Milliseconds matter. Reliability is absolutely non-negotiable.

Euronext. This is where I got inside a major European stock exchange. Order matching engines, market surveillance systems, broker connectivity. When you place a trade on Euronext, it goes through systems like the ones I helped build. This is where you truly understand how markets work — not from charts, but from the actual mechanics.

Societe Generale. One of Europe's top investment banks. I was on the trading floor, building infrastructure for the trading desks. Risk management systems, high-frequency connectivity, real-time position monitoring. Working alongside traders, quants, and risk managers every single day. You absorb an incredible amount of knowledge in that environment.

Brevan Howard. One of the world's leading macro hedge funds. This is the top tier — where every basis point counts and technology is the competitive edge. Building and maintaining trading systems at this level requires absolute precision. The standards are as high as they get in the industry.

Over the years, my role evolved naturally. Starting as a systems engineer building ultra-low-latency infrastructure. Then senior developer, designing critical systems for exchanges and banks. Moving into technical architecture, leading complex distributed systems. And eventually technical leadership, driving architecture decisions at the enterprise and fund level.

Let me put some numbers on it. Almost 25 years in the financial industry. Four or more major institutions — Thomson Reuters, Euronext, Societe Generale, Brevan Howard. Global market coverage across equities, derivatives, fixed income, and more. And dozens of critical systems built from the ground up.

Quick quiz. What does an exchange's order matching engine do? Option A, it predicts stock prices. Option B, it matches buy and sell orders in real time. Option C, it calculates company earnings. Or option D, it sends trade alerts to investors. The answer is B. The matching engine is the absolute core of every exchange. It pairs buy orders with sell orders at the best available price, often in microseconds. And yes, I've worked on these systems.
Chapter three. From infrastructure to trading. Here's where it gets interesting — how building trading systems for institutions translates into a unique edge as an independent trader and analyst.

Most traders see the screen — the charts, the candles, the indicators. But after years building the systems behind that screen, you see something completely different. You see order flow, market microstructure, latency effects, how liquidity actually works. That perspective changes everything about how you approach the markets.

Let me show you the difference. A typical retail trader sees price charts and indicators, follows news and social media tips, uses their broker's basic screener, and reacts to market moves. With an infrastructure background, you understand order flow and market microstructure, you know how data feeds work and what latency really means, you build custom screening algorithms, and you anticipate market mechanics instead of just reacting.

Over the years, I built my own personal trading toolkit. A custom algorithmic scanner that runs multiple strategies across multiple markets. Automated signal detection covering US, European, and Asia-Pacific markets every single day. A backtesting framework using real historical data. Automated risk management and position sizing. And most importantly — public retrospectives with fully transparent hit rates.

Here's the real edge, and it's not what most people think. It's not about having a secret indicator or a magic formula. It's about systematic process, proper risk management, and tools that remove emotion from decision-making. That's exactly what institutional trading desks do. And that's exactly what Market Watch brings to you.

Another quiz. What is the biggest advantage of a systematic trading approach? Option A, it guarantees profits. Option B, it removes emotional bias from decisions. Option C, it only works for hedge funds. Or option D, it requires no market knowledge. The answer is B. A systematic approach doesn't guarantee profits — nothing does. But it removes the emotional rollercoaster that causes most retail traders to buy high and sell low.
Chapter four. Market Watch — the vision. Let me tell you what this project is all about and why I believe it can help you become a better, more disciplined trader.

Here's what Market Watch delivers. Daily market briefings packed with real data, not opinions. An algorithmic scanner that produces 10 A-plus setups every single trading day. Deep stock analyses using institutional-grade metrics. Weekly macro reviews covering US, European, and Asian markets. And free educational content from beginner to advanced — like this video right here.

Let me be very clear about what we do and what we don't do. We do data-driven analysis, we maintain a transparent track record, we publish public retrospectives, and we provide free tools and education. What we don't do — we never promise guaranteed returns, we don't sell signals or subscriptions, we don't hide our methodology, and we never give financial advice.

Transparency is everything. Every single scanner pick is tracked. Every retrospective is published publicly. You can verify our hit rate yourself — go check it on the website. No cherry-picking, no hiding the losses. If a pick gets stopped out, you'll see it right there in the data.

If you want to explore, head over to articles dot market dash watch dot x y z. Browse the daily briefings, check the scanner picks, read the deep analyses. Everything is free, everything is transparent. And subscribe to this channel — every week we release videos breaking down markets, strategies, and trading education.
I'll leave you with this thought. In trading, the edge isn't in the signal — it's in the process. Thanks for watching, and I'll see you in the next video.
